title: Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Pipelines Distorts Annotation, Evaluation, and Benchmarking

scope.included: AILuminate安全判定的误差方差分解
scope.excluded: Arena与其他基准的口径争议
scope.study_summary: 同一回答材料跨judge、提示、温度与重复，测SAFE/UNSAFE判断的稳定性
scope.scope_basis: 最终reason、accepted review及qualifying_unit的限定范围；不继承旧候选单元的宽泛范围

reading.limits: 本轮逐篇核对既有最终纳入范围并定向读取以下方法/测量/控制段落；不是重新通读整篇全文。

facts.description: 141个prompt×SUT回答项目来自36题×4SUT剔除3拒答；5提示×3温度×3judge×8重复共50760次，分析项目、judge、提示温度及交互的方差。

evidence.excerpt:
4.1       Safety: Judge Disagreement Dominates
We first illustrate the variance decomposition using AILuminate v1.0 [Ghosh et al., 2025], a safety
benchmark from MLCommons. The benchmark assesses whether LLM responses cross safety lines
across 12 hazard categories (hate speech, self-harm, violent crime, etc.). Most items are unambigu-
ously safe (94% safe rate) and the variance concentrates on the 6% of borderline cases where judges
disagree about whether a refusal is adequate. We decompose the variance across judges, prompts,
temperatures, items, and their interactions, based on 36 DEMO prompts (3 per category) crossed
with responses from Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.1, DeepSeek Chat v3.1, and Grok 4.1 Fast (141 items
after dropping 3 SUT refusals), scored under 5 prompt variants × 3 temperatures × 3 judges ×
8 replications = 50, 760 calls.
The decomposition (Figure 3(a)) identifies the judge panel itself as the dominant lever, contributing
43.8% of Var(θ̂) at the operational design (N =141, V =5, M =3, H=3, R=8). Item×judge inter-
action adds another 16.7%. In other words, judge choice shifts the headline rate and panel members
disagree about which specific items are safe.7 Aggregating across the three judges in the panel cuts
the safety SE by 38% because the model design-sensitivity σλ2 and the item×judge interaction σαλ   2

both shrink as 1/M when the projection averages over M judges (Eq. 3).

facts.description: 方法采用交叉随机效应REML；对设计配置下的估计量方差报告judge份额及item×judge交互；多judge聚合改变SE。

evidence.excerpt:
Estimation uses REML [Jiang, 1996] via lmer [Bates et al., 2015] on a crossed random-effects
specification. The full formula, pilot-design thresholds, and parametric-bootstrap-CI guidance for
small facet counts are in SI Appendix, Sections C and L.

4         Empirical Demonstrations
We apply the TEE decomposition across three empirical domains in the main text: binary safety clas-
sification (AILuminate), multiple-choice QA (MMLU), and pairwise model comparison validated
against human votes (Chatbot Arena). For the safety and Arena demonstrations, we decompose
variance across judges, treating each (prompt, SUT-response) pair as an item, while in MMLU there
is no judge and we decompose variance across SUTs scored against the answer key (SI Appendix,
Section C). Section 4.4 then quantifies the gaming surface single-configuration benchmarks expose.
In the SI, we provide a political affinity annotation demonstration (Section I.1) with a 9-annotator
human baseline, a Likert vs pairwise scoring comparison (Section H), and a pilot validation showing
that a small sample recovers the qualitative D-study guidance of a 4.5× larger full run (Section I).
